intro_html: Everything you love about taco night in one loaded skillet. Lean beef, seasoned black beans, corn, and zucchini simmer together, then get finished with a little melty cheddar. It runs about $5.94 a serving (at everyday cost) with a big 52 grams of protein and makes 14 filling bowls.
cost_closing_html: About $5.94 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings brings 52 grams of protein and 636 calories, a genuinely loaded bowl.
upsell_html: Taco night flavor with the budget math working in your favor, all from one pan. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Canned black beans are one of the best cheap protein boosters you can buy. Stock up on canned beans when they hit their lowest price.
Buy your cheese in blocks and shred it yourself. Block cheese costs less per ounce than pre-shredded and melts better too.
Zucchini and canned corn stretch the beef and cost little. Lean on cheap vegetables to bulk up the skillet without adding much cost.
make_it: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Stir in the chili powder to season the meat.
Add the black beans, corn, diced zucchini, and tomato sauce and simmer until the zucchini is tender.
Stir in a little cooked rice to round out the skillet.
Sprinkle the shredded cheddar over the top and let it melt.
